clusters.section: ADR 0008 (Consequences); ADR 0001 rule 8; ADR 0002 rule 3; ADR 0003; 05 5.4; 10 10.2 item a; 12 12.4; 12 12.9
clusters.title: ADR 0008 chose to leave the review and merge-gate claims of ADR 0001 rule 8, ADR 0002 rule 3, ADR 0003 and four spec sections standing beside their negation ('as measured on 2026-10-08'), with no Supersedes link, against ADR 0001 rule 3 (stale content is deleted, not caveated).
clusters.scenario: An agent implementing T005 reads 12 12.4's merge row ('one approving review ... code-owner review for ask-first paths') and, in the same cell, that the ruleset requires none; it treats the approval line as a barrier and the PR body cites ADR 0001 rule 8 as the guarantee; a reviewer of ADR 0003 approves an agent-only merge believing the pairing check exists.
clusters.change: Spec part: in 10 10.2 item a, 12 12.4 and 12 12.9 delete the sentences that state a required code-owner or approving review and leave 'The merge requirements, and what they are worth against the sandbox token, are in 05 5.4.'; 05 5.4 keeps the one measured statement. Record part: one short new ADR, 'Record that no review is required to merge', dated 2026-10-08, that supersedes in part ADR 0003 (the review requirement) and amends ADR 0001 rule 8 and ADR 0002 rule 3, each of the three gaining a Status line 'Superseded in part by ADR 0009 for the review requirement'; ADR 0001 rule 7 gains that partial-supersede Status form so tools/ci sequences can check it.
clusters.cost: Deletions in three sections, one short record, three Status lines, one rule 7 clause.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it reverses ADR 0008's recorded choice 'We do not rewrite them' and adds a decision record on the decisions surface. Recommendation: accept; the spec-side deletions (10 10.2 item a, 12 12.4, 12 12.9) can be applied in the same write pass once the record is approved. R8-adr-12 (ADR 0001's deferral count) rides in the same record.

clusters.title: The runtime ledger is a v1 feature with no success criterion, no journey, no 00 0.5 row and no 'not in v1' alternative in ADR 0006, yet it sits on the build path before romeu run.
clusters.scenario: The first user's first run waits on three stores, two mounts, an ingest in four commands, I31 to I33, six residual-risk rows and twelve deferred rows for records no step of 09 reads; 08 8.2 already records hook failures in julieta state.
clusters.change: Either move the ledger out of v1 as one index Deferred row ('the runtime ledger (13; ADR 0006 stays Accepted as the design); until then julieta state (08 8.2) and the command's stderr are the record; reopened by the first lesson in docs/lessons.md naming a sandbox failure julieta state could not reconstruct, or the second machine'), with 13 kept as a designed-not-built page like 06 6.6 and the ledger parts of 03 3.3, 04 4.2, 04 4.4, 08 8.5, doctor and I31 to I33 removed; or keep it and give ADR 0006 the 'not in v1' alternative with its reason and 00 0.5 its row.
clusters.cost: A maintainer decision; about a page of deletions, or one alternative paragraph and one row.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it changes the scope (00 0.5) and a decision record (ADR 0006). Recommendation: defer the ledger out of v1 as stated, per the last-responsible-moment rule; the stated cost of waiting (events before it exists are not recorded, one recreate per project for the mounts) is small next to its v1 footprint. Decide together with R8-adr-15.

clusters.title: Check mechanism is written as prose with pinned versions, commit ids and function names (10 10.2, about 330 lines; ADR 0007, about 300 lines; ADR 0001's rules) while tools/ci and mise.lock are the truth and nothing holds them equal, and accepted records are never rewritten.
clusters.scenario: mise.lock bumps golangci-lint, or lintEnv is renamed; the lint row of 10 10.2 and ADR 0007 still describe the old checkers; an agent implements against the row and the fixture test fails for a reason the spec cannot explain; a reader who trusts ADRs over the spec implements the stale mechanism.
clusters.change: Add to 12 12.5: 'A record holds the decision, the alternatives and the consequences. Mechanism, tool versions and code identifiers belong to the spec or to tools/ci, which the record links; a later record that touches the same ground moves them out.' In 10 10.2 replace each pinned version in prose (mise 2026.10.3, revive v1.17.0, testifylint v1.6.4, golangci-lint 2.14.0, fsfe/reuse:6.2.0, cab976e) with a pointer to mise.lock or the workflow file that pins it, and add one sentence at the head of the step detail: 'Where this text and tools/ci differ, tools/ci is right and this text is the defect.' No generator and no new docs rule now; ADR 0007 and ADR 0001 are trimmed only by the next record that supersedes them. The stale Q25 pointer in ADR 0007 is handled by R8-adr-5.
clusters.cost: One rule in 12 12.5, about six version strings replaced by pointers, one sentence.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form stated in change: the 12 12.5 rule, version strings in 10 10.2 replaced by pointers to their pin files, and the precedence sentence; the generated docs/reference/ci.md and the version-string docs rule are not added (one mechanism less; reopen if a stale 10 10.2 row misleads an implementation).

clusters.section: 05 5.4; S1; J1; 10 10.2 (Release and bootstrap); ADR 0008 decision 6
clusters.title: Release signing exists only as a prohibition (ADR 0008 decision 6: the credential is outside GitHub, signing is an operator step) while S1's evidence says the attestation 'signed them' and no page says what is signed, with which tool, where it is published or how a user verifies it.
clusters.scenario: v1.0.0 ships with checksums.txt and an attestation; the operator never signs anything because no step says to; an incident later asks whether any release was signed and the answer is that the spec forbade the wrong way and never described the right one.
clusters.change: Recommended branch: 10 10.2 'Release and bootstrap' states 'v1 publishes no artifact signature beyond checksums.txt and the provenance attestation; a signature is a deferred decision', S1 and 05 5.4 drop 'signed', and the index gains a Deferred row 'artifact signing; until then checksums and provenance attestation (J1 verifies both); reopened by the first user or packager asking for a signature'. Other branch: name the signed artifact, the tool, the publication location and the J1 verification command.
clusters.cost: A decision on the release ask-first surface; a paragraph and one row.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it decides the meaning of ADR 0008 decision 6 and the release ask-first surface. Recommendation: the no-signature-in-v1 branch with the deferred row, which matches the last-responsible-moment rule and removes the false 'signed' from S1.

clusters.section: ADR 0007 (Threat model); index: Deferred decisions; plan.md
clusters.title: ADR 0007 defers the two pre-tools/ci escapes (an untracked go.work in the tree or a parent directory, a caller GOFLAGS such as -overlay) to Q25 and to a plan row 'whether agents push from a second account' that exists in neither plan.md nor the index; Q25 was decided by ADR 0008 on 2026-10-07, so the trigger fired, nothing reopened it, and ADR 0008's inventory of texts it leaves stale omits ADR 0007.
clusters.scenario: The hook changes later for another reason, or an agent's branch leaves a go.work in a parent of the maintainer's clone path; the host hook's go run executes replaced code; nobody reopens the two escapes because the only record is a sentence in an accepted ADR pointing at a row that does not exist, the case 'a deferral without a row is an oversight' names.
clusters.change: Add one row to index: Deferred decisions: 'Deferred: starting tools/ci from .githooks/pre-push so that an untracked go.work and the caller's GOFLAGS cannot act on go run (ADR 0007, Threat model). Until then: the hook runs go run on the tree as checked out, and the pull request's diff review is the only guard. Reopened by: the next change to .githooks/pre-push. Its first trigger, Q25, fired on 2026-10-07 (ADR 0008) and was not acted on.' Then fix ADR 0007's pointer by a one-line note in the next record (or a dated Status note) 'the deferral row cited in Threat model is the index row on the hook start; see ADR 0008', and add ADR 0007 to ADR 0008's list of texts left by pointer. Option to close it now instead: the hook starts tools/ci with GOWORK=off and GOFLAGS unset.
clusters.cost: One table row, one pointer line in a record; or two environment variables in the hook.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: the pointer fix touches accepted records (ADR 0007, ADR 0008) and the close-now option touches the hook, an ask-first checks surface. The index row itself stays inside the spec and can be applied now. Recommendation: close it now with GOWORK=off and GOFLAGS unset in the hook (two variables, cheaper than keeping the row alive), recorded with the ADR 0007 pointer note; otherwise apply the row as written. Raised independently by both noise-probe pairs (L2 and L2b, L13 and L13b) and by nine lenses in all.

clusters.section: ADR 0008 (Context); 05 5.4; index: Deferred decisions; J1; J2; 06 6.4
clusters.title: ADR 0008's Context, and the 05 5.4 and deferred rows written from it, describe the sandbox the product is developed in (operator's full token, signing key plus a GitHub authentication key) without saying so, which contradicts 06 6.4's one-key socket for a romeu sandbox and leaves the product user with no guidance to narrow the token per project.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter reads 05 5.4 as a property of romeu's sandboxes and declines the product, or follows J1 with a personal token so every sandbox reaches every repository and gist of the account; an implementer relaxes 06 6.4 to admit two keys because the ADR says two are forwarded.
clusters.change: Head of 05 5.4's token rows and the two deferred rows from ADR 0008: 'These rows describe the sandbox this repository is developed in today, which romeu does not yet manage. A romeu-managed sandbox forwards one key through signing.agentSocket (06 6.4), and its GitHub token is the github@<project> binding (Q13).' J1 step 5 and J2: 'Prefer one fine-grained token per project, limited to that repository and the scopes it needs.' ADR 0008 itself is not edited; 05 5.4 is the one place decision 2 names.
clusters.cost: About forty words in 05 5.4 and the index, one sentence in two journeys.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: the sentence changes how an accepted risk in 05 5.4 is scoped. Recommendation: accept as written; no ADR change is needed because ADR 0008 decision 2 makes 05 5.4 the single statement. Found by both L13 and L2b (each a member of a noise-probe pair whose partner did not raise it).

clusters.title: The only control over the operator's token is a habit (read the GitHub security log at each sitting) whose coverage the record calls unverified, which cannot attribute an action to the agent, reviewed 'every 2 autonomous work sessions' that nothing counts, and whose collision with the first principle (no mechanism resting on memory) is not named as the ADR 0005 collision is.
clusters.scenario: An agent adds a deploy key and a webhook to a neighbouring repository; the operator's next log read shows nothing (coverage) or an action under their own name (attribution); the habit lapses after a few sittings and the 2-session trigger never fires because no one counted.
clusters.change: Read GitHub's documentation of the personal-account security log for merge, tag, ruleset, deploy-key and webhook events and record the result with its date in 05 5.4, as item d was recorded. In ADR 0008 Consequences, by the next record: name the collision ('decision 5 is a habit, which the first principle does not count as a control; accepted by name on <date>') and replace 'every 2 autonomous work sessions' with an event a tool sees (each handoff checkpoint written to docs/HANDOFF.md, or the first release-candidate tag only). Add the maintainer's host to the stated reach.
clusters.cost: One documentation read, a dated paragraph, two sentences in a record.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it changes ADR 0008 decision 5 and deferred item 1 and the accepted risk in 05 5.4. Recommendation: do the documentation read now (it is a measurement, cheap), name the collision, and make the review trigger the handoff checkpoint; skip the six-line checklist until the log read shows a gap.

clusters.title: Deferred triggers have no reader outside review rounds, which end with v1: many fire only when a person notices ('the maintainer observes it', 'written as an issue', 'the operator saying so'), several are machine-detectable but no row names its detector, although ADR 0005 Consequences asks for exactly that.
clusters.scenario: After v1.0.0 the first outside PR arrives, or doctor warns about ledger size for months, or golangci-lint is bumped in mise.toml; the rows those events reopen sit unread because no review round is scheduled and 'nothing else reminds anyone'.
clusters.change: In the preamble of index: Deferred decisions add: 'After the review rounds end, the table is read at each release, as a step of the release pull request whose Evidence names the rows whose event happened since the last release, and on the first issue or pull request from an outside account.' In each row whose trigger a check already detects (doctor's size warning, a mise.toml bump, a dora field, romeuMs over the S8 budget), append '(seen by <check>)' to the trigger cell, as ADR 0005 Consequences already asks. Rewrite 'the operator saying so' as an event. No new column, no sequences clause, no release-notes section.
clusters.cost: One preamble sentence, a few trigger cells edited.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form stated in change: the reader-after-v1 sentence and '(seen by ...)' on the rows that already have a detector; the fourth column, the sequences check and the release-notes section are not added. ADR 0005 is not changed, since its Consequences already ask for the detector. The token row's session trigger is left to R8-adr-7, which needs the operator.

clusters.section: index: Decide at the last responsible moment; ADR 0005 rule 1
clusters.title: The carve-out 'a security invariant, a merge gate and anything a later step depends on are needs of the start' is open-ended: anything becomes a need of the start once a later section is written to depend on it.
clusters.scenario: The ledger (13) is depended on by salvage records, retire and doctor; dora by three rows of 12 12.9; each became a dependency by the text that introduced it, so the principle cannot cut what its carve-out admits.
clusters.change: Narrow the index sentence to 'a security invariant, a merge gate, and anything a step of the first-day path (J1 to J3, J5, J6) depends on; a dependency that exists only because a later section was written does not count', mirrored in ADR 0005 rule 1 by a superseding note.
clusters.cost: Two sentences and a superseding note.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: the index sentence restates ADR 0005 rule 1, so narrowing it changes a decision record. Recommendation: accept; it is the rule that makes R8-adr-2 and R8-adr-14 decidable.

clusters.title: ADR 0001 rule 7 requires contiguous ADR numbers and tools/new adr takes the next free one, so the twenty or so records due in v1 collide when written concurrently, and rule 9's cite-by-number multiplies the cost of each renumber.
clusters.scenario: T028 and T027 both scaffold ADR 0009 in one week; the later renames the file, the title line and every first mention; the plan avoids it by making T096 to T101 a six-deep serial chain at the end of the critical path.
clusters.change: In a superseding note to ADR 0001 rule 7: keep uniqueness, drop contiguity ('numbers are unique; a gap is allowed'), checked by tools/ci sequences. No reservation table.
clusters.cost: One sentence by supersession, one relaxed clause in sequences.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it amends an accepted record (ADR 0001 rule 7) and a check. Recommendation: the drop-contiguity form, which deletes a constraint instead of adding a reservation table; it can share the record of R8-adr-1.

clusters.title: The skills, the only documents written for the agent, fall under no rule of the documentation standard: rule 1 excludes SKILL.md, rule 13 checks commands in README and guides only, rule 16 is review, and only plan T078 adds a command-name test the spec does not require.
clusters.scenario: A julieta flag is renamed; the handoff skill still tells the agent the old form; tools/ci docs passes; every /handoff fails until someone notices.
clusters.change: In 10 10.2's docs step add: 'Command lines in skills/*/SKILL.md are checked against the command definitions, flags included, and the headings the handoff skill names against handoff write's validator.' This makes T078's test a spec requirement; ADR 0001 is not changed (the spec may check more than the standard requires).
clusters.cost: One sentence in 10 10.2; the check T078 already plans.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form stated in change: the requirement goes in 10 10.2, not into ADR 0001 by a superseding record.

clusters.title: ADR 0001 Consequences says 'Three things are deferred' while the index holds four rows citing ADR 0001 rule 5 (the linter and spell-checker choice too), and no front-matter field ties a hand-written page to the release or probe it was last verified against.
clusters.scenario: A reader counts deferrals from the ADR and misses one.
clusters.change: In the record of R8-adr-1 (or the next record amending ADR 0001), list the four deferred rows. The 'verified:' front-matter key is not added now.
clusters.cost: One sentence in a record already proposed.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: the count lives in an accepted record. Recommendation: fold the corrected list into the R8-adr-1 record; drop the 'verified:' key until a stale guide is found (the index is the authoritative list, so the miscount misleads only a reader of the ADR).

clusters.title: Rule 13 fixes one committed file, e2e/scenarios/commands.yaml, that every host-facing command task appends to, so phase 4 tasks conflict on it.
clusters.scenario: T043, T045, T047, T048 and T050 each add lines for their journey; the file conflicts on every second merge of phase 4.
clusters.change: No mechanism now. Add to 02 2.1 one sentence: 'commands.yaml is grouped by journey, one block per journey, so concurrent additions touch different hunks; splitting it into e2e/scenarios/commands/J<n>.yaml is deferred', with an index Deferred row reopened by 'the first phase-4 merge whose conflict in commands.yaml needs more than taking both sides'.
clusters.cost: One sentence and one deferred row.
clusters.resolution_text: State as a limit: grouped-by-journey hunks keep conflicts textual; the per-journey split waits for a conflict that costs more than a rebase. ADR 0001 rule 13 is unchanged.

clusters.title: tools/ci dora, a five-metric delivery tool with its own schema, trailer and release asset, is a v1 deliverable for a one-contributor repository with no release, while ADR 0004 itself says nothing is lost by waiting.
clusters.scenario: ADR 0004: 'every run reads the whole history, so nothing is lost by the wait'; 12 12.10: until the first release the five metrics are empty; the tool still lands at ci-release and gates the release candidate.
clusters.change: Move tools/ci dora to index: Deferred decisions: 'until then gh pr list --json by hand and the review judge the three rows of 12 12.9 that cite it; reopened by the third deployment or the first lesson that wants a delivery number'. Keep ADR 0004 Accepted as the design and keep the Fixes-release trailer form check in pr (its data cannot be backfilled).
clusters.cost: One row; the plan loses T089 and one release.yml step; three 'Enforced by' cells in 12 12.9 change to review.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it changes the v1 scope (00 0.5) of a deliverable a decision record adopted. Recommendation: defer as stated; ADR 0004's own argument supports it.

clusters.title: Parts of the ledger were accepted without being decided: six starting values 'the maintainer has not read one by one', a design 'accepted as a whole', and two residual risks that 'came with the design the maintainer accepted'.
clusters.scenario: A reviewer cannot tell a considered risk from an inherited one; the block acceptance is how a feature the start does not need got in.
clusters.change: Either the maintainer decides the two risks and the six values by name (one quoted line each), or 05 5.4 marks the two rows 'inherited, undecided' and 13 13.8 marks the values 'proposed, undecided'.
clusters.cost: Eight one-line decisions, or two words per row.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it changes accepted risks (05 5.4). Recommendation: decide with R8-adr-2; if the ledger leaves v1, the two rows and six values leave with it and nothing needs marking.

clusters.title: The Open questions table holds items in the wrong state: Q25 is decided and still listed; Q4, Q6, Q12, Q13 and Q14 have a default taken and only 'maintainer' to settle them; Q9 (Homebrew tap later) and Q23 are deferrals without a trigger in the Deferred table.
clusters.scenario: ADR 0005 defines the two tables as two states; a reader cannot tell what is open, and T101 records the maintainer rows only at the end of the plan.
clusters.change: Remove Q25 from Open questions (decided by ADR 0008). Mark Q4, Q6, Q12, Q13 and Q14 'decided (default kept); record pending T101'. Move Q9's Homebrew tap and Q23's credential to Deferred decisions with triggers 'the first install report that asks for brew' and 'the first private workload registry'.
clusters.cost: Table edits only; no new ADR now.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form stated in change: table edits only; the five ADRs stay with T101 rather than moving to the docs module's first task.

clusters.title: One person is 'operator', 'maintainer', 'developer' and 'user' depending on the page, none of the four is in the vocabulary, and the only sentence relating them is in ADR 0008 Context.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter reads 'the maintainer's approval' in 05 5.3 and 'the operator decided' in 05 5.4 and concludes the product has two roles they must find or invent.
clusters.change: Add to 01 1.7: operator (the person who runs romeu on a host, owns host settings and answers gates); maintainer (the person who merges and releases this repository); developer or user (the operator as 00 0.2 counts them); and 'Today one person holds both the operator and the maintainer role.' Then a word pass so each page uses each word only in its sense.
clusters.cost: Three rows, one sentence, a word pass.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed; ADR 0008 is not edited (its Context already uses both words consistently with these rows).

clusters.title: Rule 13 exempts the checksum and attestation commands of the install and verify guides because release.yml 'runs that verification', but it runs tools/release verify, not the guide's command lines.
clusters.scenario: The guide ships a wrong --signer-workflow path, and nothing ever runs the lines users copy.
clusters.change: In 10 10.2, state that tools/release verify reads its command lines from the same e2e/scenarios/commands.yaml entry the guide renders, so rule 13's exemption becomes true as written.
clusters.cost: One sentence; one data source shared by two consumers.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in 10 10.2 only, which makes ADR 0001 rule 13's claim true without changing the record.

clusters.title: The gate tool is specified in final form (about 27 subcommands, a closed workflow grammar, a meta-lint, a 20-rule documentation standard adopted before a page exists) with no mark of which steps the first-day path needs.
clusters.scenario: 10 is the longest page of the spec for a product whose objective has five bullets; each check is defended, the count is not.
clusters.change: In 10 10.2 mark the steps the first-day path needs (fast, hygiene, workflows minimal, unit, invariants) and say once that the rest land with their first input, the rule the plan already follows. ADR 0001's rules are not split.
clusters.cost: Wording; no mechanism removed.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the 10 10.2 marking only; the ADR 0001 rule split is dropped, since rules already land with the first page that needs them.

clusters.title: Rule 12 fixes the README's level-2 headings with a check that fails an extra heading, and the list has no place for what romeu stores on the machine or how to stop using it.
clusters.scenario: The writer of T095 wants a short 'Your data' section; tools/ci docs fails it and the text is folded into 'trust model' or dropped.
clusters.change: Add 'data and uninstall' between 'trust model' and 'links' in rule 12's order and in tools/ci/headings.yaml, with its outline in 12 12.8 (link to the store table and the J14 guide).
clusters.cost: One heading in the rule, the headings file and 12 12.8.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it amends ADR 0001 rule 12 on the decisions and checks surfaces. Recommendation: defer to T095, the first input that needs it, and fold it into the R8-adr-1 record if that record is written first.

clusters.title: ADR 0006's alternatives treat every deletion as history rewriting and do not consider the owner discarding a project's entries or the whole ledger on the host, so there is no recorded reason for forbidding it.
clusters.scenario: A later reviewer has to decide whether doctor may tolerate a hand-removed project and finds only 'nothing is ever edited or deleted'.
clusters.change: When ADR 0006 is next superseded, or by the record that decides L16-4, add the alternative 'operator removal of a project's entries or of the whole ledger' with its decision and why.
clusters.cost: A paragraph and a maintainer decision.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it adds an alternative to an accepted record. Recommendation: moot if R8-adr-2 takes the ledger out of v1; otherwise decide with L16-4.

clusters.title: The classes of what the operator's token can reach omit repositories of other organizations the account is a member of, such as an employer's, and 05 5.4 reuses the sentence for every project.
clusters.scenario: A sandbox for a personal project, steered by issue text, opens a pull request in or reads a private repository of the employer organization the operator belongs to.
clusters.change: Add to the token rows of 05 5.4: 'including repositories of every organization the account is a member of'. ADR 0008 is not edited, since 05 5.4 is the one statement (decision 2).
clusters.cost: One clause in 05 5.4.
clusters.resolution_text: Needs the operator: it widens an accepted risk in 05 5.4 by naming a reach the acceptance did not list. Recommendation: accept the clause; it is a fact of the account, and R8-adr-6's per-project token advice is its mitigation.
